titulo: Sounds, alphabet and first words: Vowels, double consonants and stress

aula.objetivo: Spell in Italian, read the letter combinations that change the sound (c, g, ch, gh, sc, gn, gli), hear double consonants and word stress, and make your first greetings, with «tu» and with «Lei».

blocos.contexto: In a café in Rome, signora Rossi meets Paolo, the barista, and young Luca. Listen first. Notice who says «Come sta?» and who says «Come stai?».

linhas.pt: — Good morning, signora Rossi! How are you?

linhas.ru: — Buongiorno, Paolo! Sto bene, grazie. E Lei?
linhas.pt: — Good morning, Paolo! I'm fine, thank you. And you?
linhas.audio: Buongiorno, Paolo! Sto bene, grazie. E Lei?

linhas.pt: — Fine, thank you. Here is your coffee.

linhas.ru: — Grazie mille! Ah, ecco Luca! Ciao, Luca! Come stai?
linhas.pt: — Thank you very much! Oh, here comes Luca! Hi, Luca! How are you?
linhas.audio: Grazie mille! Ah, ecco Luca! Ciao, Luca! Come stai?

linhas.ru: — Buongiorno, signora! Sto bene, grazie. E Lei?
linhas.pt: — Good morning, signora! I'm fine, thank you. And you?
linhas.audio: Buongiorno, signora! Sto bene, grazie. E Lei?

linhas.ru: — Bene, bene. Paolo, un cappuccino per Luca, per favore?
linhas.pt: — Fine, fine. Paolo, a cappuccino for Luca, please?
linhas.audio: Bene, bene. Paolo, un cappuccino per Luca, per favore?

linhas.pt: — Right away! Here you are, Luca.

blocos.explicacao: STEP 1: Italian vowels are always clear and full. The final «e» of «bene», «latte» and «come» sounds «eh», never «ay» and never a weak «uh». The final «o» of «tavolo» and «otto» is a pure «oh», with no «w» glide at the end as in English «go». STEP 2: every double consonant is held longer. Make a tiny pause before it. Say «otto» as «OHT-toh». STEP 3: the double letter changes the meaning. «Pala» is a shovel, «palla» is a ball. «Caro» means dear, «carro» is a cart. «Nono» means ninth, «nonno» is grandfather. «Sete» is thirst, «sette» is the number seven. So listen carefully and write both letters.
blocos.comparacao: in English, unstressed vowels shrink to a weak «uh» («banana» sounds «buh-NA-nuh»), and long vowels glide («go» sounds «goh-oo»). A double letter is not heard either: «summer» has one «m» sound. Italian keeps every vowel full and pure, and you really hear the double consonant, like the two «k» sounds in «bookcase».

tabela.como: full and clear: e, o, a, i, u
held longer, with a short pause before it

erros.motivo: The final «e» is a short, clear «eh», never «ay» and never «uh».
The double letter changes the word: shovel or ball.
The number has two «t». With only one, «sete» means thirst.

blocos.explicacao: STEP 1: the strongest syllable of a word is almost always the second-to-last: «amíco», «mámma», «bélla». STEP 2: in some words it falls one syllable earlier: «télefono», «álbero». Listen to the audio and repeat. STEP 3: the written accent appears almost only at the end of a word, to mark the strong vowel: «città», «caffè», «perché», «università». STEP 4: in one-syllable words, the accent tells two words apart. «È», with an accent, is the verb «is». «E», without an accent, is «and». «Sì», with an accent, is «yes». «Là», with an accent, is «there». STEP 5: the «h» is never pronounced: «ho», «hotel», «hanno». STEP 6: «qu» sounds «kw», like in «quick», with the «u» heard: «quattro» (KWAHT-troh), «questo» (KWEH-stoh). STEP 7: «z» sounds «ts» or «dz», depending on the word: «grazie» (GRAHT-see-eh), «zucchero» (DZOOK-keh-roh). There is no simple rule. Learn it with the audio.
blocos.comparacao: English also has a strong syllable in every word, but never marks it in writing. Italian marks it only when it falls on the last vowel. And unlike English, the Italian «h» is always silent, even in «hotel».

tabela.como: at the end of the word
the accent tells two words apart

erros.motivo: The accent at the end of the word marks the strong syllable.

blocos.explicacao: STEP 1: Italian has two ways of addressing a person. STEP 2: «tu» is for friends, family, children and young people. You ask «Come stai?». STEP 3: «Lei» is for strangers, older people and work situations. You ask «Come sta?». STEP 4: here, «Lei» does not mean «she». It is a form of respect, and the verb takes the «she» form: «sta». STEP 5: when in doubt, use «Lei». Nobody is offended because you are polite. Culture: if the other person wants, they will suggest it themselves: «Diamoci del tu», which means «let's use tu with each other».
blocos.comparacao: English has only «you» for everyone. In Italian you choose between «tu» and «Lei» from the very first sentence, a bit like choosing between «Hi, Tom» and «Good morning, Mr Smith».

exemplos.pt: How are you? (to a stranger, formal)
I'm fine, thank you. And you? (formal)

erros.motivo: With a lady you address formally, you use «Lei», so «sta».

itens.explicacao: Listen to the long consonant: «palla» has two «l» and means ball. «Pala» is a shovel, with a short «l».
Listen to the long «nn» and the final «o». «Nonna» would end in «a» and mean grandmother.
Listen to the ending: «sta» is the formal question, for someone you call «Lei». «Stai» ends in «i».
Write: sette. Listen to the long «tt»: there are two «t».
Write: Sto bene, grazie. Listen to the full «e» at the end of «bene» and the «tsee-eh» of «grazie».

itens.enunciado: How does the final «e» of «bene» sound?
itens.explicacao: Italian vowels are clear and complete. The final «e» is always «eh».
The double consonant changes the meaning: «pala» is a shovel and «palla» is a ball.
With «sta» the question is formal, for someone you call «Lei».

blocos.enunciado: Read out loud, with full vowels: «Buongiorno! Come sta? — Sto bene, grazie. E Lei?» Then, with a friend: «Ciao! Come stai? — Bene, grazie. E tu?»
Read out loud: cena, che, gente, spaghetti, scuola, gnocchi, famiglia. What is the sound of each letter group?
